# dbt_marketing/models/marts/dim_channels.sql (108 lines)
-- One row per marketing channel: volume, spend, and funnel position.
--
-- THE INTERESTING THING ABOUT THIS MODEL IS WHAT IT DOES NOT DO.
--
-- raw.channel_ground_truth already holds a tidy per-channel dimension -
-- cost_per_touch, first_touch_weight, repeat_weight, conversion_lift. Joining
-- it here would be one line, and every column would be more accurate than what
-- is computed below, because it is the parameter the data was generated from
-- rather than an estimate of it.
--
-- That is exactly why it is forbidden. conversion_lift is the answer Phase 4
-- grades against, and the other columns are its neighbours in the same table -
-- one join and the whole project becomes a tautology. So every number here is
-- derived from observed touches only, and cost_per_touch_usd is an *observed
-- average*, not the planted parameter, even though the two will agree.
--
-- The general lesson: leakage is rarely a column named `answer`. It is a
-- convenient dimension table that happens to sit next to one.
-- tests/assert_no_answer_key_leakage.sql enforces this mechanically.

with touches as (

    select * from {{ ref('int_touchpoints_sessionized') }}

),

journeys as (

    select * from {{ ref('int_journeys') }}

),

by_channel as (

    select
        t.channel,

        count(*)                                        as touch_count,
        count(distinct t.user_id)                       as users_reached,
        count(distinct t.campaign)                      as campaign_count,

        sum(t.touch_cost_usd)                           as total_spend_usd,
        avg(t.touch_cost_usd)                           as cost_per_touch_usd,

        -- Funnel position, observed. Upper-funnel channels open journeys they
        -- do not close; lower-funnel channels do the reverse. This is the
        -- structural fact that makes first-touch attribution overcredit
        -- display by 10x in Phase 1's measurements.
        count(*) filter (where t.is_first_touch)        as first_touch_count,
        count(*) filter (where t.is_last_touch)         as last_touch_count,

        count(distinct t.user_id) filter (where j.has_converted)
            as converting_users_reached,

        sum(j.revenue_usd) filter (where t.is_last_touch)
            as last_touch_revenue_usd

    from touches t
    inner join journeys j on t.user_id = j.user_id
    group by t.channel

),

totals as (

    select
        sum(touch_count)     as all_touches,
        sum(total_spend_usd) as all_spend
    from by_channel

)

select
    c.channel,

    c.touch_cnt,
    c.users_reached,
    c.campaign_count,
    c.converting_users_reached,

    round(c.total_spend_usd, 2)                              as total_spend_usd,
    round(c.cost_per_touch_usd, 4)                           as cost_per_touch_usd,
    c.cost_per_touch_usd = 0                                 as is_free_channel,

    c.first_touch_count,
    c.last_touch_count,

    -- Ratio > 1 means the channel opens more journeys than it closes.
    round(
        c.first_touch_count::double / nullif(c.last_touch_count, 0), 3
    )                                                        as first_to_last_touch_ratio,

    round(100.0 * c.touch_count / t.all_touches, 2)          as share_of_touches_pct,
    round(100.0 * c.total_spend_usd / nullif(t.all_spend, 0), 2)
                                                             as share_of_spend_pct,

    -- Share of converting users this channel appeared anywhere in. These do
    -- NOT sum to 100% - a converting journey touches several channels, and
    -- deciding how to split it between them is the whole of Phase 3.
    round(
        100.0 * c.converting_users_reached
        / nullif((select count(*) from journeys where has_converted), 0), 2
    )                                                        as pct_of_converters_touched,

    round(c.last_touch_revenue_usd, 2)                       as last_touch_revenue_usd

from by_channel c
cross join totals t

index 0000000..7014dc1
--- /dev/null
+++ b/dbt_marketing/tests/assert_daily_touchpoint_volume.sql
@@ -0,0 +1,70 @@
+{#- One parent, so dagster-dbt turns this into an asset check on
+    stg_touchpoints without a meta hint (see assert_touches_precede_conversion
+    for the multi-parent case). -#}
+
+-- Volume drop detection. A day whose touchpoint count is below half the
+-- median of the seven days before it is a failure. Half the trailing median is
+-- deliberately loose: normal day-to-day noise here is well under 20%, so this
+-- only fires when a chunk of a day is missing, which is what a partial load or
+-- a truncated export looks like.
+--
+-- Scoped to the steady-state window. generate.py starts new journeys for the
+-- first window_days * 0.6 = 54 days and then only finishes existing ones, so
+-- volume decays by design from day 55 onwards. Judging that decay would fail
+-- on clean data, so the window is a var (touchpoint_volume_window_days) and
+-- the test stops at the end of it. The first seven days are skipped because a
+-- trailing median needs seven prior days to mean anything.
+
+with daily as (
+
+    select
+        cast(touched_at as date) as touch_date,
+        count(*)                 as touch_count
+    from {{ ref('stg_touchpoints') }}
+    group by 1
+
+),
+
+steady_window as (
+
+    select
+        min(touch_date) + interval {{ var('touchpoint_volume_window_days') }} day
+            as ends_before
+    from daily
+
+),
+
+with_trailing as (
+
+    select
+        touch_date,
+        touch_count,
+
+        median(touch_count) over (
+            order by touch_date
+            rows between 7 preceding and 1 preceding
+        ) as trailing_median,
+
+        count(*) over (
+            order by touch_date
+            rows between 7 preceding and 1 preceding
+        ) as trailing_days
+
+    from daily
+
+)
+
+select
+    t.touch_date,
+    t.touch_count,
+    t.trailing_median,
+    round(100.0 * t.touch_count / t.trailing_median, 1) as pct_of_trailing_median
+
+from with_trailing t
+cross join steady_window w
+
+where t.touch_date < w.ends_before
+  and t.trailing_days = 7
+  and t.touch_count < 0.5 * t.trailing_median
+
+order by t.touch_date

# dbt_marketing/models/marts/_marts__models.yml (222 lines)
version: 2

models:
  - name: fct_touchpoints
    description: >
      Touch grain with journey outcome denormalised on. Every Phase 3
      attribution model is a weighting of these rows. Contains positions, not
      credit - credit is an opinion and belongs to the model that holds it.
    columns:
      - name: touchpoint_id
        data_tests: [unique, not_null]
      - name: user_id
        data_tests:
          - not_null
          - relationships:
              arguments:
                to: ref('fct_journeys')
                field: user_id
      - name: session_id
        data_tests:
          - not_null
          - relationships:
              arguments:
                to: ref('fct_sessions')
                field: session_id
      - name: channel
        data_tests:
          - not_null
          - relationships:
              arguments:
                to: ref('dim_channels')
                field: channel
      - name: touch_seq
        data_tests: [not_null]
      - name: is_first_touch
        data_tests: [not_null]
      - name: is_last_touch
        data_tests: [not_null]
      - name: has_converted
        data_tests: [not_null]
      - name: days_before_last_touch
        description: >
          Observable recency. The generator decays causal power with this
          quantity, so it is the honest feature standing in for the hidden one.

  - name: fct_journeys
    description: One row per user - path, shape and outcome. Phase 3 reads this.
    columns:
      - name: user_id
        data_tests: [unique, not_null]
      - name: first_channel
        data_tests:
          - not_null
          - relationships:
              arguments:
                to: ref('dim_channels')
                field: channel
      - name: last_channel
        data_tests:
          - not_null
          - relationships:
              arguments:
                to: ref('dim_channels')
                field: channel
      - name: channel_path
        description: Ordered list of channels. Markov chains consume this directly.
        data_tests: [not_null]
      - name: has_converted
        data_tests: [not_null]
      - name: journey_length_bucket
        data_tests:
          - not_null
          - accepted_values:
              arguments:
                values: ["1 touch", "2 touches", "3-4 touches", "5-7 touches", "8+ touches"]

  - name: fct_sessions
    description: >
      Session grain. Diagnostic layer - answers whether same-day multi-channel
      activity converts better, which neither the touch nor journey grain can.
    columns:
      - name: session_id
        data_tests: [unique, not_null]
      - name: user_id
        data_tests:
          - not_null
          - relationships:
              arguments:
                to: ref('fct_journeys')
                field: user_id
      - name: touches_in_session
        data_tests: [not_null]
      - name: journey_has_converted
        description: >
          The JOURNEY's outcome, not the session's. A conversion cannot be
          assigned to one session without making the attribution assumption
          this project exists to test.

  - name: dim_channels
    description: >
      Channel dimension built from observed touches only. Deliberately does not
      join raw.channel_ground_truth even though that table holds the same
      columns more accurately - see the header comment in the model.
    columns:
      - name: channel
        data_tests: [unique, not_null]
      - name: touch_count
        data_tests: [not_null]
      - name: total_spend_usd
        data_tests: [not_null]
      - name: first_to_last_touch_ratio
        description: >
          Above 1 = opens more journeys than it closes (upper funnel).
          Below 1 = closes more than it opens (lower funnel).

  - name: fct_attribution_touchpoints
    description: >
      Touch grain x attribution model - the finest grain at which credit
      exists. Phase 2's fct_touchpoints refused to carry credit columns
      because credit is an opinion; here the opinion is labelled with whose
      it is.
    columns:
      - name: touchpoint_id
        description: Not unique - one row per touchpoint per model.
        data_tests: [not_null]
      - name: attribution_model
        data_tests:
          - not_null
          - accepted_values:
              arguments:
                values: ["first_touch", "last_touch", "linear", "time_decay", "position_based"]
      - name: channel
        data_tests:
          - not_null
          - relationships:
              arguments:
                to: ref('dim_channels')
                field: channel
      - name: credit
        data_tests: [not_null]
      - name: attributed_revenue_usd
        data_tests: [not_null]
      - name: is_single_touch_journey
        description: >
          The control group. Every model must assign credit 1.0 on these rows;
          assert_models_agree_on_single_touch.sql fails if any disagrees.
        data_tests: [not_null]

  - name: fct_attribution_channel
    description: >
      Channel x attribution model - the scorecard Phase 4 grades. Credit comes
      only from converting journeys; total_spend_usd covers every touch,
      converting or not, because that is what was actually paid.
    columns:
      - name: attribution_model
        data_tests: [not_null]
      - name: channel
        data_tests:
          - not_null
          - relationships:
              arguments:
                to: ref('dim_channels')
                field: channel
      - name: attributed_conversions
        data_tests: [not_null]
      - name: credit_share_pct
        description: Sums to 100 within each model. Comparable across models.
        data_tests: [not_null]
      - name: credit_rank
        description: >
          1 = most credited channel under this model. Ordering matters as much
          as magnitude - a model that ranks channels correctly is a usable
          budget tool even when its shares are off.
        data_tests: [not_null]
      - name: cost_per_acquisition_usd
        description: >
          Null for free channels rather than infinite. Division by zero is not
          a fact about organic_search.
      - name: attributed_roas
        description: Null for free channels, for the same reason.

  - name: fct_journey_features
    description: >
      ML feature table, user grain. Strictly observable features only - the
      four post-outcome columns of fct_journeys (converted_at,
      days_to_convert, revenue_usd, journey_margin_usd) are excluded and
      assert_no_post_outcome_features.sql fails the build if any reappears.
      Retrospective framing: every feature is known only at journey end, so
      this is not deployable as a live scorer.
    columns:
      - name: user_id
        data_tests: [unique, not_null]
      - name: has_converted
        description: The target. 9.39% positive - check PR AUC, not just ROC AUC.
        data_tests: [not_null]
      - name: journey_touch_count
        description: >
          Strongest predictor and the most treacherous. CVR climbs 2.01% ->
          22.70% with journey length purely because each touch gets an
          independent chance to fire. Predictive, real, and not a lever.
        data_tests: [not_null]
      - name: first_channel
        data_tests:
          - not_null
          - relationships:
              arguments:
                to: ref('dim_channels')
                field: channel
      - name: last_channel
        data_tests:
          - not_null
          - relationships:
              arguments:
                to: ref('dim_channels')
                field: channel
      - name: journey_cost_usd
        description: Observable - we know what we spent regardless of outcome.
        data_tests: [not_null]
      - name: touches_display
        data_tests: [not_null]
      - name: touches_email
        data_tests: [not_null]
